title: The Cooking Choe Starring David Choe and Harry Kim Aka Guam Cruise

segments.x: Thumbs up everyone. We're cooking. Sometimes you're on the road and you don't have too much money and you want to eat as much food. The thing about this is you eat all the chicken. It looks clean, but there's grease in there. We want to trap that grease, that fried chicken flavor. You cook the ramen

in the microwave. You mix it up. You let the juices touch the sides. Pour this into a big gulp size. These are pieces of pork that are deep fried. When you buy anything at the place that starts with seven and ends with 11, there's as much free condiments. See, we filled up an entire tub of ramen with chili and

some jalapenos. You could hear the crunchy shells are getting soft now. You know, presentation has a lot to do with cooking. Put that in the middle like a fondue tray. The pork rinds are softening and expanding. Get some chili ramen action. There's not really anybody I know who doesn't like mayo. So, let's
squeeze some in there. M. Man, that's good.

editorial.summary: This official 55-second fragment presents an improvised low-budget road meal: leftover fried-chicken grease, microwaved ramen, chili, jalapeños, pork rinds and mayonnaise arranged with comic food-show attention to presentation. It is useful evidence for Thumbs Up's cooking/road-survival format, but it is not evidence of a complete Cooking Choe episode, a safe standardized recipe, a 7-Eleven policy or named dialogue. The title credits David Choe and Harry Kim; the auto transcript itself supplies no speaker labels.
